Thought: I need to determine the stability of the three cations represented in SMILES notation. The stability of carbocations is influenced by factors like resonance and hyperconjugation. Let me analyze each structure.

The three cations are:
1. C=C[CH+]C=C - This is an allylic carbocation with two C=C groups adjacent to the positive charge
2. C[CH+]C=C - This is an allylic carbocation with one C=C group adjacent to the positive charge
3. C[CH+]CC - This is a secondary carbocation with no adjacent C=C groups

Carbocation stability is generally increased by:
1. Resonance stabilization - when the positive charge can be delocalized through resonance
2. Hyperconjugation - when adjacent C-H bonds can interact with the empty p orbital
3. Inductive effects - electron-donating groups increase stability

For allylic carbocations, the positive charge can be delocalized through resonance with the adjacent C=C double bond. The more extensive the resonance, the more stable the carbocation.

C=C[CH+]C=C has two C=C groups adjacent to the carbocation center, allowing for more extensive resonance stabilization than C[CH+]C=C which has only one C=C group.

C[CH+]CC has no adjacent C=C groups, so it cannot be stabilized by resonance, only by hyperconjugation. This makes it the least stable of the three.

Therefore, the order from most stable to least stable is:
C=C[CH+]C=C (most stable due to resonance with two C=C groups)
C[CH+]C=C (intermediate stability due to resonance with one C=C group)
C[CH+]CC (least stable, no resonance stabilization)

This corresponds to option A.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
